newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end higher buoyed by other markets.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end higher buoyed by other markets.

text.p: Italian shares ended higher on Thursday reflecting a firmer start to Wall Street and record levels on London stocks, but the FIB30 futures contract showed less impressive gains as some caution took hold.

Support for the market's rally also came from comments by Prime Minister Romano Prodi who said in a newspaper interview that he saw no need for a rise in European interest rates, including Italy, despite the continued strength in the dollar. This boosted banking shares with Rolo Banca suspended limit up.
The all-share Mibtel index ended up 0.89 percent at 14,822 while the Mib30 blue chip index was up 0.7 percent at 22,453.

Rolo Banca, controlled by Credito Italiano, was suspended on the Milan bourse when the share price exceeded the 10 percent upside limit after rising strongly in heavy volume all morning. It soon shed its gains and ended off 0.25 percent at 20,300 lire

Montedison was another share to end lower, off 0.59 percent at 1,171 lire, after its 50-50 Montell joint venture with Shell showed second quarter operating profits down at $76 million from $99 million previously.
Most blue chips ended higher with energy group ENI up 1.0 percent at 10,772, Fiat 1.65 percent higher at 6,031 lire and Pirelli 0.8 percent firmer at 5,012 lire.
